label: input token j at original-phase positions 3-6
explanation: Fires on every step where the input is the letter j during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t = 3, 4, 5 or 6, and nowhere else. Never fires on other tokens, on j at positions 0-2 or 7-8, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (even when j is fed back as input). Magnitude depends on position: highest at t = 4 and t = 5 (top examples about 1.75 are j at t = 4), lower at t = 3 and t = 6. Earlier tokens and sequence length have little effect beyond that. Dev split: precision, recall and F1 are all 1.0.

issues: None found. On the test split the predicate is exact: precision 1, recall 1, F1 1, mass recall 1, and misses --split test lists 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Dev profile supports every claim. All activations are in the original phase; the delimiter and copy phase have 0 active steps, and recall_idx >= 0 has 0 active steps. Only in_tok j is active, with a rate of 0.249 among j steps, which matches j at positions 3-6 being about 4/16 of j occurrences. Positions t=0-2 and t>=7 have 0 active steps.
Magnitude claim checks out. Activation mass per active step is highest at t=4 (0.389/13685) and t=5 (0.297/11147), roughly twice the value at t=3 (0.222/16294) and t=6 (0.092/8238).

The variation in rate by L comes only from how many of positions 3-6 exist: L=3 has none, and L=4 has only t=3. The firing rate within a given orig_idx is flat at about 0.033. So 'sequence length has little other effect' holds.
